column1: # Example shot list: PluginCity Advanced Pre-Orders for WooCommerce.
# One line per readme caption, in the readme's order. Copy this into a plugin
# repo, point the paths at that plugin's screens, and run
#   scripts/screenshot.sh path/to/screenshots.tsv dist/screenshots
# against a harness that has already been seeded.
# The ids are not written here. {{product.slug}} and {{order.key}} are filled in
# from what the seed recorded, so reseeding the shop cannot quietly point a shot
# at a different screen. A placeholder the seed never recorded stops the run.
# A placeholder resolves to a number, so it belongs where a URL wants a number:
# the admin's post= and id=. A storefront permalink already names the product by
# the slug the seed gave it, and screenshot-1 says so in full. Putting a
# placeholder there photographs /product/11/, which is a 404 that crops and
# saves like any other page.
# The caption is the last column and nothing in the capture reads it. It is here
# because the caption and the screen it describes are one editorial decision, and
# filing them apart is how a set comes to illustrate the wrong sentence.
# screenshot-1 says who is looking, and the storefront shots are the ones that
# have to. Without a prefix a shot is taken as the administrator, which is right
# for wp-admin and wrong for a page meant to show a customer's screen -- an
# administrator is let through WooCommerce's Coming soon page and a shopper is
# not, so a set taken entirely as the administrator can photograph a shop no
# customer can reach.
# An 'allow' line would go here too, naming one shot and one request that is known
# to fail and known to change nothing on the screen. None is needed for these
# four, which is the usual answer.
# name
